subject: Clarify commit bucket smoothing + streaming metering language
messages:

To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement <contracts@atlashealth.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify: commit buckets + streaming billing for proof-of-concept

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week — AtlasHealth engineering and ML were impressed with the latency profile. Before we proceed to a short POC, procurement asked for a quick note on two items that will affect our internal cost model:

1) Commit buckets: how you smooth usage across months for promos/credits (we have variable traffic)
2) Streaming calls: how "billable tokens" are accounted for streaming sessions and any rounding rules when clients close a stream mid-response

Can you send a short description we can attach to the SOW? Procurement also asked if there is language you can accept around a true-up cadence and whether partial-month smoothing is possible.

Attached is a one-pager with our expected POC pattern.

Appreciate a short response we can share internally.

—Molly

Attachments: 20261116-Atlas_ask_summary.pdf (PDF, 120KB)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 12:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify: commit buckets + streaming billing for proof-of-concept

Hi Molly — great to hear. Quick summary below to attach to the SOW; I copied Aditya (pricing) and Laura (legal) so they can confirm operational/contract language.

High-level answers for procurement:
- Commit buckets: we support monthly or quarterly commits. For variable traffic we offer a smoothing option that allocates a committed token balance across the commit period and allows one month of negative variance (carry-forward) to be recovered in the next month up to the committed amount.
- True-up cadence: standard is monthly true-up with a 14-day invoicing cycle; we can do quarterly true-ups for larger contracts on request.
- Streaming tokens: billable tokens are defined as total tokens generated + total tokens received from client input for the session. For open streaming sessions we bill tokens when they are emitted. If a stream is closed mid-response, the partial generation is billed proportionally to the tokens emitted; we do not round up to the next full response token by default.

Operational notes:
- If you choose smoothing, the monthly unit price is applied against the effective smoothed bucket; overages above the committed bucket will be billed at the overage rate.
- For short POC periods (<30 days) we can offer a pro-rated commit bucket rather than a full-month commit.

I'll let Aditya and Laura propose draft SOW language that procurement can drop into their template.

Thanks — talk soon,
Soojin

Subject: RE: Clarify: commit buckets + streaming billing for proof-of-concept

Molly / Soojin — adding a few contract-first bullets you can paste into the SOW or a redline. I'm intentionally precise on definitions to avoid future disputes.

1) Billable unit definition: "Billable Token" means any discrete token as counted by Redwood's metering system, including client-provided tokens (prompt/context) and tokens produced by the model. For streams, tokens are recorded in real time; the recorded token count at stream closure is the billable amount.
2) Rounding: token-level metering is exact (no rounding up) for emitted tokens. For billing display we present tokens rounded to the nearest whole token, but invoicing uses actual token counts aggregated per invoice period.
3) Smoothing / bucket carry-forward: for monthly smoothing, unused committed tokens roll forward for one month only and expire thereafter. Negative variance (overage) can be covered by the following month's committed volume up to 100% of that month's commit; any remainder is billed as overage.
4) Pro-rate for partial-month POC: commit buckets can be pro-rated by days in period; credit applied immediately to the POC month.

If these look good I'll draft short clauses for the MSA (metering section) and the SOW (billing appendix). Laura — any legal constraints on the wording above?

- Aditya
Head of Pricing, Redwood Inference

Thanks — a couple of small asks from legal to make the language procurement-friendly:

- Please add a short sentence about "metering disputes": customer has 30 days from invoice date to raise a metering dispute, Redwood will provide token-level logs and an audit window of 90 days.
- Explicitly call out that "smoothing" is optional and must be selected in the SOW; otherwise standard monthly commits apply.
- For the rounding statement, change "no rounding up" to "billing reflects actual recorded tokens aggregated by invoice period; minor display rounding may occur in dashboards but is for presentation only."

I'll draft a two-paragraph SOW appendix and attach it as a redline.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Molly Turner <molly@atlashealth.com>

Cc: procurement <contracts@atlashealth.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify: commit buckets + streaming billing for proof-of-concept

Thanks — that addresses most of our questions. Procurement pushed back on two points and attached requested redlines:

1) They want smoothing to allow a 2-month carry-forward window (instead of 1 month) for the pilot phase only.
2) They asked that the metering dispute window be 45 days instead of 30.

I've attached our suggested contract redline (Word doc). Would Redwood accept the pilot exceptions with the following constraints: pilot smoothing 2-month carry-forward, dispute window 45 days for pilot invoices only, and a firm no-auto-roll clause (we won't auto-enroll smoothing after pilot).

Attachments: 20261117-redlines-streaming-metering.docx

—Molly

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Molly Turner <molly@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, procurement <contracts@atlashealth.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 17:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify: commit buckets + streaming billing for proof-of-concept

Molly — thanks for the redlines. Quick summary and proposed path:

- Pilot exceptions: Redwood can accept a one-time pilot amendment: 2-month carry-forward for unused pilot commit only, and 45-day metering dispute window for pilot invoices. These exceptions will be explicit in the SOW and expire at the end of the pilot.
- No-auto-roll: agree — smoothing must be opt-in and will not auto-enroll post-pilot.
- Metering logs & audit: Redwood will provide token-level logs for the 90-day audit window.

Next steps: Laura will produce the brief SOW appendix (including the pilot amendment language). Aditya will add a short billing appendix that lists the exact invoicing cadence and overage rate for the POC commit. Molly — if procurement confirms the redline as-is we'll issue a pilot SOW and begin the POC onboarding.

I'll follow up with the drafted appendix and a proposed SOW tomorrow.

Best,
